title: Friend Groups
difficulty: Medium
position: 12
complexity: O(n + m)
=== statement
There are `n` people, numbered 1 to `n`, and a list of friendships. Friends of friends are in the same group, however long the chain. How many groups are there? Someone with no friends is a group on their own.

One chain of friends can include everyone, so deep recursion may run out of stack.
=== input
The first line has `n` and `m`. Each of the next `m` lines has two people `a b` who are friends.
=== output
Print the number of groups.
=== constraints
1 <= n <= 65536
0 <= m <= 65536
1 <= a, b <= n
=== sample
5 3
1 2
2 3
4 5
--- expected
2
=== sample
4 0
--- expected
4

1 0
